claims.claim: The ratio between κ and λ light chain (LC)-expressing B cells varies considerably between species.
claims.source: The ratio between κ and λ light chain (LC)-expressing B cells varies considerably between species.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific citation to experimental data in this manuscript.

claims.claim: Kidins220 was identified as an interaction partner of the BCR.
claims.source: We recently identified Kinase D-interacting substrate of 220 kDa (Kidins220) as an interaction partner of the BCR.
claims.evidence: References prior work by the authors (Fiala et al., 2015).

claims.claim: In vivo ablation of Kidins220 in B cells resulted in a marked reduction of λLC-expressing B cells.
claims.source: In vivo ablation of Kidins220 in B cells resulted in a marked reduction of λLC-expressing B cells.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and referenced prior publication (Fiala et al., 2015).

claims.claim: Kidins220 knockout B cells fail to open and recombine the genes of the Igl locus, even in genetic scenarios where the Igk genes cannot be rearranged.
claims.source: Kidins220 knockout B cells fail to open and recombine the genes of the Igl locus, even in genetic scenarios where the Igk genes cannot be rearranged or where the κLC confers autoreactivity.
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figures 2 and 3 showing germline transcript levels and κ-KO mouse experiments.

claims.claim: Igk gene recombination and expression in Kidins220-deficient B cells is normal.
claims.source: Igk gene recombination and expression in Kidins220-deficient B cells is normal.
claims.evidence: Supported by data in Figure 1 and Figure 2 showing similar Igk germline transcripts and κLC expression between CTRL and B-KO.

claims.claim: Kidins220 regulates the development of λLC B cells by enhancing the survival of developing B cells.
claims.source: Kidins220 regulates the development of λLC B cells by enhancing the survival of developing B cells and thereby extending the time-window in which the Igl locus opens and the genes are rearranged and transcribed.
claims.evidence: Supported by apoptosis data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and BCL2 rescue experiments in Figures 4 and 5.

claims.claim: Kidins220 guarantees optimal pre-BCR and BCR signaling to induce Igl locus opening and gene recombination during B cell development and receptor editing.
claims.source: Further, our data suggest that Kidins220 guarantees optimal pre-BCR and BCR signaling to induce Igl locus opening and gene recombination during B cell development and receptor editing.
claims.evidence: Supported by signaling data in Figure 8 showing reduced ERK phosphorylation and ROS levels, and receptor editing experiments in Figures 6 and 7.

claims.claim: The BCR is composed of two immunoglobulin heavy chains and two Igκ or Igλ light chains.
claims.source: Antigen recognition in B cells is mediated by the B cell antigen receptor (BCR), composed of two immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy chains (HC) and two Igκ or Igλ light chains (LC).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about BCR structure.

claims.claim: The BCR forms a complex with the associated Igα and Igβ heterodimer to transmit signals for B cell development, proliferation, survival, and activation.
claims.source: They form the BCR complex together with the associated Igα and Igβ heterodimer to transmit signals for B cell development, proliferation, survival, and activation.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about BCR signaling.

claims.claim: Each B cell expresses a BCR with a given specificity acquired by progressive rearrangement of V, D, and J gene segments in the bone marrow.
claims.source: Each B cell expresses a BCR with a given specificity, which is acquired by a progressive rearrangement of the variable (V), joining (J) and, in case of the HC, diversity (D) gene segments of the BCR HC and LC loci in the bone marrow (BM) (reviewed in Clark et al., 2014; Herzog et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to review articles.

claims.claim: RAG1 and RAG2 proteins are the key enzymes that facilitate V(D)J recombination.
claims.source: The key enzymes that facilitate V(D)J recombination are recombination-activating gene 1 (RAG1) and RAG2 proteins (Oettinger et al., 1990; Schatz et al., 1989).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: V(D)J recombination is initiated at the pro-B cell stage.
claims.source: V(D)J recombination is initiated at the pro-B cell stage (Rolink et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: An in-frame rearrangement at the HC genes leads to the expression of a µHC that binds to the λ5 and VpreB components of the surrogate light chain.
claims.source: An in-frame rearrangement at the HC genes leads to the expression of a µHC that is binding to the λ5 and VpreB components of the surrogate light chain (Karasuyama et al., 1990; Reth et al., 1985; Tsubata and Reth, 1990).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The pre-BCR complex is first expressed on large pre-B cells.
claims.source: Together with the Igα/β signaling subunits, these chains form the pre-BCR complex, which is first expressed on large pre-B cells.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about B cell development.

claims.claim: Signals from the pre-BCR and IL-7 receptor induce a proliferative burst followed by cell cycle attenuation, promoting LC V- to J-gene segment rearrangement in the small pre-B cell stage.
claims.source: Signals from the pre-BCR and the interleukin (IL)–7 receptor (IL-7R) induce a proliferative burst that is followed by cell cycle attenuation, promoting LC V- to J-gene segment rearrangement in the small pre-B cell stage (Flemming et al., 2003; Ma et al., 2010; Mandal et al., 2009; Ochiai et al., 2012; Reth et al., 1985; Reth and Nielsen, 2014).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: A productive rearrangement leads to the pairing of the pre-existing HC with the newly generated LC, forming the IgM-BCR expressed first on immature B cells in the BM.
claims.source: A productive rearrangement leads to the pairing of the pre-existing HC with the newly generated LC, forming the IgM-BCR expressed first on the immature B cells in the BM (reviewed in Herzog et al., 2009; Matthias and Rolink, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to review articles.

claims.claim: LC locus opening and recombination during B cell development and receptor editing is dependent on transcription factors including Ikaros, Aiolos, IRF-4, IRF-8 and E2A.
claims.source: LC locus opening and recombination during B cell development and receptor editing (a process changing the specificity of the BCR by secondary LC VJ-gene rearrangements) is dependent on transcription factors including Ikaros, Aiolos, interferon regulatory factor (IRF)–4, IRF-8 and E2A (Bai et al., 2007; Beck et al., 2009; Inlay et al., 2004; Johnson et al., 2008; Lazorchak et al., 2006; Lu et al., 2003; Ma et al., 2006; Ma et al., 2008; Mandal et al., 2009; Pathak et al., 2008; Quong et al., 2004; Stadhouders et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Genetic mouse models individually lacking some transcription factors show impaired LC locus opening, affecting λLC expression more severely.
claims.source: Genetic mouse models individually lacking some of these transcription factors show impaired LC locus opening, affecting λLC expression more severely (Beck et al., 2009; Lu et al., 2003; Pathak et al., 2008; Quong et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The activity of transcription factors regulating LC locus opening is directly or indirectly regulated by pre-BCR and BCR signaling.
claims.source: The activity of these transcription factors is directly or indirectly regulated by pre-BCR and BCR signaling.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the literature and supported by subsequent citations.

claims.claim: Mice lacking a signaling competent pre-BCR or BCR, or lacking signaling molecules downstream including SLP65, BTK and PLCγ2, are characterized by an altered LC expression.
claims.source: Mice lacking a signaling competent pre-BCR or BCR, or lacking signaling molecules downstream of the pre-BCR or BCR including the adapter protein SLP65, Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) and phospholipase Cγ2 (PLCγ2), are characterized by an altered LC expression (Bai et al., 2007; Dingjan et al., 2001; Hayashi et al., 2004; Kersseboom et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Mice deficient in SLP65 show reduced LC germline transcripts especially from the Igl locus.
claims.source: Specifically, mice deficient in SLP65 show reduced LC germline transcripts especially from the Igl locus (Hayashi et al., 2004; Kersseboom et al., 2006; Stadhouders et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The absence of BTK severely reduces Igl germline transcripts and LC expression.
claims.source: Likewise, the absence of BTK, a kinase that is recruited by SLP65, severely reduces Igl germline transcripts and LC expression (Dingjan et al., 2001; Kersseboom et al., 2006; Stadhouders et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The concurrent ablation of both SLP65 and BTK abrogates Igk and Igl germline transcription and BCR surface expression.
claims.source: The concurrent ablation of both SLP65 and BTK abrogates Igk and Igl germline transcription and BCR surface expression (Kersseboom et al., 2006; Stadhouders et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: PLCγ2 is recruited to SLP65, regulating the calcium signaling downstream of the pre-BCR and BCR.
claims.source: PLCγ2 is recruited to SLP65, regulating the calcium signaling downstream of the pre-BCR and BCR (Hashimoto et al., 2000; Xu et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: PLCγ2-knockout mice show a strong reduction of λLC B cells and a mild reduction of Igk germline transcripts.
claims.source: PLCγ2-knockout (KO) mice show a strong reduction of λLC B cells and a mild reduction of Igk germline transcripts (Bai et al., 2007; Xu et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The combined deficiency of BTK and PLCγ2 almost completely abrogated LC expression.
claims.source: The combined deficiency of BTK and PLCγ2 almost completely abrogated LC expression (Xu et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Pre-BCR signaling is important for the induction of LC VJ-gene rearrangement at both LC loci (Igk and Igl).
claims.source: Pre-BCR signaling is important for the induction of LC VJ-gene rearrangement at both LC loci (Igk and Igl).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the preceding discussion of signaling molecule knockouts.

claims.claim: The ratio between the usage of the two LCs diverges greatly among species.
claims.source: However, the ratio between the usage of the two LCs diverges greatly among species (Sun et al., 2013) and the regulation of their differential expression is still not fully understood.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: The primary B cell repertoire in mice is dominated by the κLC that is roughly ten to 20 times more frequent than the λLC.
claims.source: The primary B cell repertoire in mice is dominated by the κLC that is roughly ten to 20 times more frequent than the λLC (McGuire and Vitetta, 1981; Sun et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: λLC B cell generation is favored when rearrangement at the Igk locus is unsuccessful, or when the immature κLC-containing BCR confers autoreactivity.
claims.source: It is generally accepted that λLC B cell generation is favored when rearrangement at the Igk locus is unsuccessful, or when the immature κLC-containing BCR confers autoreactivity (Luning Prak et al., 2011; Nemazee, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Extending the life-span of B cell precursors by overexpression of BCL2 promotes the generation of λLC B cells.
claims.source: Extending the life-span of B cell precursors by overexpression of the anti-apoptotic protein B cell lymphoma 2 (BCL2), promotes the generation of λLC B cells (Ait-Azzouzene et al., 2005; Derudder et al., 2009; Dingjan et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Limiting B cell survival by genetically abrogating the NF-κB signaling pathway results in mice with a reduced amount of λLC B cells.
claims.source: In line with this, limiting B cell survival by genetically abrogating the NF-κB signaling pathway, results in mice with a reduced amount of λLC B cells (Derudder et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: The generation of λLC B cells mainly depends on the ability and kinetics of the LC locus opening, the life-span of developing B cells, and the efficiency of receptor editing during tolerance induction.
claims.source: Based on these observations, the generation of λLC B cells mainly depends on (i) the ability and kinetics of the LC locus opening, (ii) the life-span of developing B cells, and (iii) the efficiency of receptor editing during tolerance induction (Derudder et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the literature and supported by citation.

claims.claim: Kidins220 was first described as Kinase D-interacting substrate of 220 kDa in neuronal cells.
claims.source: Kidins220 was first described as Kinase D-interacting substrate of 220 kDa in neuronal cells (Iglesias et al., 2000; Kong et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: As a scaffold protein, Kidins220 is implicated in multiple cellular processes like survival, proliferation and receptor signaling, including the antigen receptors of T and B cells.
claims.source: As a scaffold protein, Kidins220 is implicated in multiple cellular processes like survival, proliferation and receptor signaling, among which are also the antigen receptors of T and B cells (Deswal et al., 2013; Fiala et al., 2015; Neubrand et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The complete genetic deletion of Kidins220 is embryonically lethal.
claims.source: The complete genetic deletion of Kidins220 is embryonically lethal (Cesca et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Conditional mb1Cre-mediated B cell specific Kidins220 KO mice showed reduced BCR signaling.
claims.source: Conditional mb1Cre-mediated B cell specific Kidins220 KO mice (B-KO) showed reduced BCR signaling, and almost complete loss of λLC B cells in the BM and periphery, with only mild effects on the κLC compartment (Fiala et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from prior work supported by citation.

claims.claim: Conditional mb1Cre-mediated B cell specific Kidins220 KO mice showed almost complete loss of λLC B cells in the BM and periphery, with only mild effects on the κLC compartment.
claims.source: Conditional mb1Cre-mediated B cell specific Kidins220 KO mice (B-KO) showed reduced BCR signaling, and almost complete loss of λLC B cells in the BM and periphery, with only mild effects on the κLC compartment (Fiala et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from prior work supported by citation and confirmed by data in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: B-cell-specific Kidins220 KO mice show an approximately 75% reduction of B cells carrying a λLC-containing IgM-BCR on the cell surface.
claims.source: Despite almost normal B cell numbers, B-cell-specific Kidins220 KO (B-KO) mice show an approximately 75% reduction of B cells carrying a λLC-containing IgM-BCR on the cell surface (Figure 1A; Fiala et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1A and prior publication.

claims.claim: 98–99% of HCs in immature B cells from CTRL and B-KO mice were annotated to the IgM isotype.
claims.source: Successful purification of immature B cells was confirmed by the annotation of 98–99% of HCs to the IgM isotype (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: In CTRL mice, 83% of all µHCs were co-expressed with the κLC, and the remaining 17% with various subclasses of the λLC.
claims.source: In the CTRL, 83% of all µHCs were co-expressed with the κLC, and the remaining 17% with various subclasses of the λLC (Figure 1C and D).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claims.claim: In B-KO B cells, the µHC was almost exclusively co-expressed with the κLC (98%) and only 2% of all cells contained a λLC.
claims.source: In contrast, in B-KO B cells, the µHC was almost exclusively co-expressed with the κLC (98%) and only 2% of all cells contained a λLC.
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claims.claim: The absence of λLC BCRs on the surface of B cells in B-KO mice reflects absent production of mRNA of Igl from all λLC subclasses.
claims.source: Thus, the absence of λLC BCRs on the surface of B cells in B-KO mice reflects absent production of mRNA of Igl from all λLC subclasses.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the sequencing data showing lack of λLC transcripts.

claims.claim: Kidins220 does not influence which V(D)J-gene is used for the µHC of the BCR.
claims.source: We obtained very strong correlations for Igh-V- and J-gene usage (r=0.97 and 0.98, respectively), suggesting that Kidins220 does not influence which V(D)J-gene is used for the µHC of the BCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Supported by correlation analysis of sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: A good correlation of the Igk-V- and J-gene usage (r=0.96 and r=1, respectively) was observed between CTRL and Kidins220-deficient cells.
claims.source: Likewise, we observed a good correlation of the Igk-V- and J-gene usage (r=0.96 and r=1, respectively) between CTRL and Kidins220-deficient cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), confirming a rather intact κLC repertoire.
claims.evidence: Supported by correlation analysis of sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: B-KO B cells showed a slightly increased use of Igkj5 (14.2%) when compared to CTRL (10%).
claims.source: Still, B-KO B cells showed a slightly increased use of Igkj5 (14.2%) when compared to CTRL (10%) (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Use of Igkj5 correlates with increased secondary Igk-V- to J-gene rearrangements.
claims.source: Use of Igkj5 correlates with increased secondary Igk-V- to J-gene rearrangements. It frequently occurs before deletion of part of the Igk locus via a recombining sequence recombination and opening of the Igl locus (Prak et al., 1994; Retter and Nemazee, 1998).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The murine Igl locus comprises one cassette including Iglv2 and Iglv3 upstream of Iglj2-c2 (λ2), and a second cassette containing Iglv1 upstream of Iglj3-c3 (λ3) and Iglj1-c1 (λ1).
claims.source: The murine Igl locus comprises one cassette including Iglv2 and Iglv3 upstream of Iglj2-c2 (λ2), and a second cassette containing Iglv1 upstream of Iglj3-c3 (λ3) and Iglj1-c1 (λ1) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Gerdes and Wabl, 2002; Sanchez et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: In mature wild type B cells, the different λLCs are used at a frequency of 62%, 31% and 7% for λ1, λ2 and λ3, respectively.
claims.source: In mature wild type B cells, the different λLCs are used at a frequency of 62%, 31% and 7% for λ1, λ2 and λ3, respectively (Boudinot et al., 1994; Sanchez et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The pattern of λLC usage (62%, 31% and 7% for λ1, λ2 and λ3) was confirmed by sequencing results for immature B cells in CTRL mice.
claims.source: This pattern was confirmed by our sequencing results for immature B cells in CTRL mice (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: The Igl-V-gene usage showed a preference for Iglv1 over Iglv3 or Iglv2, independent of the presence of Kidins220.
claims.source: The Igl-V-gene usage showed a preference for Iglv1 over Iglv3 or Iglv2, independent of the presence of Kidins220 (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Kidins220-deficient B cells showed a relative increase of Iglv1-gene usage (88% vs 59% in CTRL).
claims.source: However, Kidins220-deficient B cells showed a relative increase of Iglv1-gene usage (88% vs 59% in CTRL) (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Both CTRL and B-KO immature B cells preferentially used the Iglj1-gene segment (44% and 69%, respectively).
claims.source: Both CTRL and B-KO immature B cells preferentially used the Iglj1-gene segment (44% and 69%, respectively).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: B-KO B cells used Iglj3 more frequently than Iglj2.
claims.source: However, B-KO B cells used Iglj3 more frequently than Iglj2.
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: In the absence of Kidins220, the genes of the second λLC cassette are favored.
claims.source: These observations suggest that in the absence of Kidins220, the genes of the second λLC cassette are favored (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the sequencing data showing increased Iglv1 and Iglj3 usage.

claims.claim: The Pearson correlation coefficient for the Igl-J-gene segments was weak in B-KO cells (r=0.51).
claims.source: Indeed, the Pearson correlation coefficient for the Igl-J-gene segments was weak in B-KO cells (r=0.51) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: In the Igl locus, VJ-gene recombination preferentially takes place within the same cassette and is almost absent between cassettes.
claims.source: In the Igl locus, VJ-gene recombination preferentially takes place within the same cassette and is almost absent between cassettes (Reilly et al., 1984; Sanchez et al., 1991).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Recombination of Iglv1 to either Iglj3 or Iglj1 was almost exclusively detected, whereas Iglv2 and Iglv3 recombined to Iglj2.
claims.source: In line with this, we almost exclusively detected recombination of Iglv1 to either Iglj3 or Iglj1, whereas Iglv2 and Iglv3 recombined to Iglj2 (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: Both CTRL and Kidins220-deficient λLC B cells showed a prominence of Iglv1-Iglj1 joins.
claims.source: Both CTRL and Kidins220-deficient λLC B cells showed a prominence of Iglv1- Iglj1 joins.
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: Both genotypes showed a clear polyclonal distribution for the κLC, but polyclonality was slightly reduced for the HC and strongly restricted for the λLC in the B-KO immature B cells.
claims.source: Both genotypes showed a clear polyclonal distribution for the κLC, but polyclonality was slightly reduced for the HC and strongly restricted for the λLC in the B-KO immature B cells (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: Supported by CDR3 frequency analysis shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: The repertoire of BCRs bearing a λLC was strongly restricted in the B-KO immature B cells.
claims.source: The analysis of paired HC-LC combinations highlighted that indeed the repertoire of those BCR bearing a λLC was strongly restricted in the B-KO immature B cells (Figure 1H).
claims.evidence: Supported by paired HC-LC CDR3 frequency analysis shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: No predispositions for potentially autoreactive BCRs as characterized by longer or more positively charged CDR3s were observed in B-KO mice.
claims.source: We did not observe any predispositions for potentially autoreactive BCRs as characterized by longer or more positively charged CDR3s within their variable domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D).
claims.evidence: Supported by CDR3 length and charge analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D.

claims.claim: The primary B cell repertoire of B-KO mice showed signs of specific clonal expansion, especially of one single clone containing the Ighv10-1-gene segment.
claims.source: Unexpectedly, the primary B cell repertoire of B-KO mice showed signs of specific clonal expansion, especially of one single clone containing the Ighv10-1-gene segment (Figure 1I).
claims.evidence: Supported by similarity network analysis shown in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: The usage of the Ighv10-1-gene segment has been previously associated with anti-DNA antibodies and herpesvirus infections.
claims.source: The usage of this Igh-V-gene segment has been previously associated with anti-DNA antibodies and herpesvirus infections (Maranhão et al., 2013; Zelazowska et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Both CTRL and B-KO showed similar frequencies of sequences defined as unproductive rearrangements (92% and 93%, respectively) from the Igh locus.
claims.source: Both, CTRL and B-KO, showed similar frequencies of sequences defined as unproductive rearrangements (92% and 93%, respectively) from the Igh locus.
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1J.

claims.claim: The frequency of sequences defined as unproductive rearrangements from the Igl and Igk loci was increased in B-KO compared to CTRL cells: 1.2 times for Igk, and 2 times for the Igl locus.
claims.source: In contrast, the frequency of sequences defined as unproductive rearrangements from the Igl and Igk loci was increased in B-KO compared to CTRL cells: 1.2 times for Igk, and 2 times for the Igl locus (Figure 1J).
claims.evidence: Supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1J.

claims.claim: Unproductive rearrangements within the Igl locus in B-KO cells were caused by a series of premature stop-codons.
claims.source: Deeper investigations revealed that these unproductive rearrangements within the Igl locus were caused by a series of premature stop-codons.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from deeper analysis of the sequencing data.

claims.claim: Genetic ablation of Kidins220 in B cells skews the primary BCR repertoire mainly due to unsuccessful production of λLCs.
claims.source: Taken together, genetic ablation of Kidins220 in B cells skews the primary BCR repertoire mainly due to unsuccessful production of λLCs.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion inferred from all the sequencing data presented.

claims.claim: CTRL and B-KO showed increasing levels of κLC+IgM-BCR+ B cells over time after IL-7 withdrawal in pro-/pre-B cell cultures.
claims.source: CTRL and B-KO showed increasing levels of κLC+IgM-BCR+ B cells over time (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: The proportion of λLC+IgM-BCR+ B cells was higher in CTRL compared to B-KO B cells at day 3 of culture after IL-7 withdrawal.
claims.source: The proportion of λLC+IgM-BCR+ B cells was higher in CTRL compared to B-KO B cells at day 3 of culture, suggesting that the in vivo phenotype is B cell intrinsic.
claims.evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Prior to LC VJ-gene rearrangement, the gene locus is opened and germline transcripts are produced.
claims.source: Prior to LC VJ-gene rearrangement, the gene locus is opened and germline transcripts are produced (also known as sterile transcripts that do not encode for any protein but are proposed to possess regulatory functions) (Engel et al., 1999; Schlissel and Baltimore, 1989).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: The relative amount of Igk germline transcript and the kinetics of induction was similar between CTRL and B-KO B cells.
claims.source: The relative amount of Igk germline transcript and the kinetics of induction was similar between CTRL and B-KO B cells.
claims.evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claims.claim: Kidins220-deficient B cells failed to induce germline transcription from the Igl locus to the levels of CTRL cells in pro-/pre-B cell cultures upon IL-7 withdrawal and in sorted pre- and immature B cells.
claims.source: However, Kidins220-deficient B cells failed to induce germline transcription from the Igl locus to the levels of CTRL cells in pro-/pre-B cell cultures upon IL-7 withdrawal and in sorted pre- and immature B cells (Figure 2C and D).
claims.evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claims.claim: The Igk germline transcripts in the CTRL cells peaked at day 2 compared to day 3 for the Igl germline transcripts.
claims.source: The Igk germline transcripts in the CTRL cells peaked at day 2 compared to day 3 for the Igl germline transcripts, in line with the findings that activation of the Igk locus precedes the Igl locus (Engel et al., 2001; Luning Prak et al., 2011; Nemazee, 2006).
claims.evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2C and established knowledge from citations.

claims.claim: LC germline transcription is dependent on the expression of E2A proteins (E12 and E47), which in turn regulate the RAG1 and RAG2 proteins.
claims.source: LC germline transcription is dependent on the expression of E2A proteins (E12 and E47), which in turn regulate the RAG1 and RAG2 proteins that are responsible for VJ-gene recombination (Beck et al., 2009; Hsu et al., 2003; Quong et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: No major differences in the expression of Tcf3 (encodes for E12 and E47), Rag1 and Rag2 mRNA were detected between CTRL and B-KO B cells shortly upon IL-7 withdrawal.
claims.source: We did not detect major differences in the expression of Tcf3 (encodes for E12 and E47), Rag1 and Rag2 mRNA as assayed by qRT-PCR between CTRL and B-KO B cells shortly upon IL-7 withdrawal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) nor in directly sorted cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claims.claim: The proportion of GFP+ cells over the 3 days upon IL-7 withdrawal was comparable between CTRL and B-KO cells in the RAG-activity reporter assay.
claims.source: The proportion of GFP+ cells over the 3 days upon IL-7 withdrawal was comparable between CTRL and B-KO cells. This suggests that RAG protein activity per se is not affected by the absence of Kidins220 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).

results.result: Kidins220 knockout in B cells results in a severe reduction of λLC-expressing B cells (approximately 75% reduction) while κLC expression remains normal. Single-cell sequencing confirmed that in B-KO mice, 98% of µHCs were co-expressed with κLC and only 2% with λLC, compared to 83% κLC and 17% λLC in controls. This skewing of the BCR repertoire is due to unsuccessful production of λLCs.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C38, C39, C41, C42, C43, and C68 are strongly supported by flow cytometry data (Figure 1A) and single-cell sequencing data (Figure 1C-D) showing consistent reduction of λLC+ B cells in B-KO mice. The data demonstrate both surface expression and mRNA transcript deficiency across all λLC subclasses.

results.result: Kidins220-deficient B cells fail to open and transcribe the Igl locus. Germline transcript analysis showed that while Igk germline transcripts were similar between CTRL and B-KO cells, Igl germline transcripts failed to reach control levels in B-KO cells both in culture and in sorted pre- and immature B cells. This effect is independent of transcriptional or functional regulation of RAG proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C73, C78, C79, and C185 are well-supported by qRT-PCR data (Figure 2C-D) showing reduced Igl germline transcripts in B-KO cells, while Igk transcripts remain normal. RAG activity reporter assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) and expression data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C) confirm that RAG machinery is not affected.

results.result: Igk gene recombination and expression in Kidins220-deficient B cells is normal. Correlation analysis showed strong correlations for Igk-V- and J-gene usage (r=0.96 and r=1) between CTRL and B-KO cells, and Igk germline transcript levels and kinetics were similar between genotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C44, C45, and C72 are supported by sequencing data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) showing high correlation of Igk gene usage and qRT-PCR data (Figure 2C-D) showing similar Igk germline transcript levels. This demonstrates specificity of the Kidins220 effect for the Igl locus.

results.result: In κ-knockout mice where all B cells must use λLC, Kidins220 is still necessary for λLC B cell development. B-KO κ-KO mice showed only 15% of the B220+IgM+ population compared to CTRL κ-KO mice, and λLC+ B cell numbers were severely reduced despite the genetic pressure to use λLC. All BCR+ B cells in κ-KO mice used λLC exclusively, but B-KO κ-KO mice failed to compensate for the loss of κLC.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C89 and C98 are strongly supported by flow cytometry data (Figure 3) showing that even when forced to use λLC (κ-KO background), B-KO mice cannot generate normal numbers of λLC+ B cells. This demonstrates that Kidins220 is essential for λLC development independent of κLC availability.

results.result: BCL2 overexpression partially rescues λLC expression in Kidins220-deficient B cells in vitro, but the rescue is incomplete. BCL2 overexpression rescued survival equally in CTRL and B-KO cells, and increased λLC+ B cells in B-KO cultures, but λLC+ B cells remained significantly reduced compared to CTRL. Additionally, Tcf3 (E47) and Rag2 mRNA transcripts were significantly reduced in BCL2-transduced B-KO cultures.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C113 are supported by survival assays (Figure 4B), flow cytometry (Figure 4C), and qRT-PCR data (Figure 4D-E) showing that BCL2 overexpression improves but does not fully rescue λLC expression in B-KO cells. The reduced Tcf3 and Rag2 expression in BCL2-rescued cells indicates Kidins220 has functions beyond survival.

results.result: BCL2 overexpression in vivo increases λLC+ B cells in CTRL mice but fails to restore λLC+ B cell numbers to control levels in B-KO mice. In BCL2-transgenic CTRL mice, both BM and splenic λLC+ B cells were expanded (sixfold for λLC vs twofold for κLC), but B-KO BCL2-transgenic mice showed significantly lower λLC+ B cell numbers than CTRL BCL2-transgenic mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C121, C127, and C128 are supported by extensive flow cytometry data from BCL2-transgenic mice (Figure 5) showing differential expansion of λLC+ vs κLC+ compartments and incomplete rescue in B-KO mice. The stronger expansion of λLC+ compartment demonstrates the survival-dependence of λLC B cells.

results.result: In κ-macroself mice (receptor editing model), Kidins220 is not required for elimination of autoreactive κLC+ BCRs but is essential for generating replacement λLC+ B cells. Both CTRL and B-KO HSC-reconstituted κ-macroself mice showed elimination of κLC+ B cells, but B-KO-reconstituted mice had significantly reduced λLC+ B cell numbers compared to CTRL-reconstituted mice, resulting in 'holes in the BCR repertoire'.
results.evaluation: Claims C131-C139, C147-C149 are supported by BM reconstitution experiments (Figure 6) showing successful elimination of κLC+ B cells in both genotypes but impaired generation of λLC+ B cells in B-KO. This demonstrates Kidins220 is dispensable for strong BCR signaling during tolerance but essential for λLC generation during receptor editing.

results.result: BCL2 overexpression combined with enforced receptor editing (κ-macroself model) fails to fully rescue λLC expression in Kidins220-deficient B cells. BCL2-expressing HSC from CTRL mice showed increased λLC+ B cells in κ-macroself recipients, but BCL2-expressing B-KO HSC did not show increased λLC+ B cells and failed to reach CTRL levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C150-C154, C158-C160 are supported by BM reconstitution data with BCL2-transduced HSC (Figure 7) showing that even the combination of prolonged survival and enforced receptor editing cannot fully rescue λLC expression in B-KO cells. This confirms Kidins220 has functions beyond survival in λLC generation.

results.result: Kidins220-deficient B cells show reduced pre-BCR signaling. B-KO mice showed reduced CD25+ cells with lower CD25 surface expression, failed to efficiently upregulate MHCII, and showed increased CD43-expressing B cells. Phosphorylation of proximal signaling molecules (SYK, SLP65) and NF-κB pathway components (p65, IκB) was unaltered, but phospho-ERK positive pre- and immature B cells were significantly reduced.
results.evaluation: Claims C163-C169 are supported by flow cytometry data (Figure 8A) showing altered surface marker expression and phospho-flow data (Figure 8B-D) showing selective reduction in ERK phosphorylation while proximal signaling remains intact. This indicates a specific defect in coupling to the MAPK/ERK pathway.

results.result: Kidins220-deficient B cells show significantly reduced ROS levels during BM development, particularly in small pre-B cells and immature B cells, while mitochondrial function appears normal. The drop in ROS from large to small pre-B cells was more pronounced in B-KO cells, and ROS remained at very low levels throughout BM development.
results.evaluation: Claims C170-C174, C177, and C178 are supported by ROS measurement data (Figure 8E) showing reduced ROS in B-KO cells across developmental stages and MitoTracker data (Figure 8—figure supplement 1) showing normal mitochondrial mass and activity. This suggests ROS reduction is due to impaired signaling rather than mitochondrial dysfunction.

results.result: BTK overexpression in pro-/pre-B cell cultures increases λLC+ B cells more than κLC+ B cells in CTRL cells, but fails to rescue λLC B cell numbers to CTRL levels in B-KO cells. This emphasizes the dual function of Kidins220 in regulating (pre-)BCR signaling and supporting B cell survival.
results.evaluation: Claims C180-C183 are supported by flow cytometry data (Figure 9) showing differential effects of BTK overexpression on λLC vs κLC B cells and incomplete rescue in B-KO cells. This provides additional evidence that Kidins220 functions through multiple mechanisms.

results.result: Kidins220 regulates λLC B cell development through two mechanisms: (1) enhancing survival of developing B cells to extend the time window for Igl locus opening and recombination, and (2) promoting optimal pre-BCR and BCR signaling via ROS and ERK to induce Igl locus opening during both homeostatic development and receptor editing.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C7, and C238 represent the main conclusions of the study and are supported by the collective evidence from survival experiments (Figures 4-5), signaling experiments (Figure 8), receptor editing experiments (Figures 6-7), and germline transcript analysis (Figure 2). The dual mechanism is demonstrated by incomplete rescue with BCL2 alone.

results.result: Single-cell BCR sequencing analysis reveals that B-KO mice have a skewed BCR repertoire with restricted λLC diversity, increased unproductive Igl rearrangements (2-fold increase), and signs of clonal expansion (particularly Ighv10-1-gene segment). The repertoire shows no predisposition for autoreactive BCRs based on CDR3 length and charge analysis.
results.evaluation: Claims C40, C50, C60-C63, C65-C67 are supported by single-cell sequencing data (Figure 1B-J) showing successful purification of immature B cells (98-99% IgM), restricted λLC repertoire, increased unproductive rearrangements with premature stop codons, and clonal expansion. The lack of autoreactive signatures is supported by CDR3 analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-D).

results.result: In B-KO mice, there is altered usage of Igl gene segments with increased Iglv1 usage (88% vs 59% in CTRL), preferential use of Iglj3 over Iglj2, and favoring of the second λLC cassette genes. B-KO cells also showed slightly increased Igkj5 usage (14.2% vs 10% in CTRL), which correlates with increased secondary Igk rearrangements.
results.evaluation: Claims C46, C51-C56, C58-C59 are supported by single-cell sequencing data (Figure 1E-F) showing differential gene segment usage patterns. The weak Pearson correlation for Igl-J-gene segments (r=0.51) in B-KO cells confirms altered recombination patterns. The biological interpretation is reasonable given the known organization of the Igl locus.

results.result: In pro-/pre-B cell cultures, both CTRL and B-KO cells show increasing κLC+IgM-BCR+ B cells over time after IL-7 withdrawal, but λLC+IgM-BCR+ B cells are higher in CTRL compared to B-KO at day 3, confirming the phenotype is B cell intrinsic.
results.evaluation: Claims C69 and C70 are supported by flow cytometry data from pro-/pre-B cell cultures (Figure 2B) showing similar κLC kinetics but reduced λLC in B-KO cells. This demonstrates the phenotype is cell-intrinsic and not due to environmental factors.

results.result: In the spleen, κ-KO mice show reduced B220+ and B220+IgM+ B cells, which is further amplified by Kidins220-deficiency (60-80% reduction in B-KO κ-KO vs CTRL κ-KO). B-KO mice show enhanced skewing toward MZ B cell differentiation, which is further enhanced in κ-KO background. While CTRL κ-KO mice compensate to ~50% of κ-sufficient levels, B-KO κ-KO mice fail to compensate.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C97 are supported by flow cytometry data from spleens of κ-KO mice (Figure 3I-Q) showing additive effects of κ-KO and Kidins220-deficiency on B cell numbers and maturation. The MZ skewing in B-KO mice is consistent with prior reports and is enhanced in the κ-KO background.

results.result: IL-7R expression is normal in B-KO mice, but IL-7R signaling via the PI3K pathway is enhanced, as shown by increased phosphorylation of AKT (S473) and FOXO1 (S256) in both pro- and pre-B cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C103 are supported by flow cytometry data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) showing normal IL-7R expression and phospho-flow data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) showing increased pAKT and pFOXO1. This suggests compensatory signaling through IL-7R pathway in the absence of Kidins220.

results.result: In BCL2-transgenic mice, the percentage of splenic B cells is slightly reduced due to T cell expansion, transitional B cells show altered proportions, MZ B cells are severely reduced, and λLC+ B cells show relative and absolute increases in both CTRL and B-KO mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C125 are supported by flow cytometry data from BCL2-transgenic mice spleens (Figure 5H-P, Figure 5—figure supplement 1H-O) showing expected effects of BCL2 overexpression on B cell subsets. These findings are consistent with prior literature on BCL2-transgenic mice.

results.result: In κ-macroself mice, BCR- B cells are increased in BM and spleen independent of Kidins220 expression, and total B cell numbers in spleen are reduced compared to non-transgenic mice. Functional tolerance is indicated by lack of κLC+ B cells in periphery, with increased λLC usage in both CTRL and B-KO groups, though λLC B cell numbers only significantly increased in CTRL-reconstituted mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C140-C145 are supported by flow cytometry data from κ-macroself reconstituted mice (Figure 6G-M, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D-H) showing expected tolerance phenotypes and differential ability to generate λLC+ B cells. The increase in BCR- cells is consistent with prior reports in this model.

results.result: Analysis of BCL2-expressing vs non-expressing cells within the same mice reveals that Kidins220-deficient λLC+ B cells benefit more from BCL2 overexpression than CTRL counterparts in WT mice, but this difference disappears in κ-macroself mice. This demonstrates that BCL2 has a greater impact on λLC than κLC B cell generation.
results.evaluation: Claims C156 and C157 are supported by flow cytometry data comparing GFP+ (BCL2-expressing) vs GFP- cells (Figure 7L-M) showing differential benefit of BCL2 on λLC vs κLC B cells. This provides direct evidence for the survival-dependence of λLC B cells.

results.result: The introduction provides established knowledge about BCR structure, V(D)J recombination, B cell development, the role of pre-BCR and BCR signaling in LC locus opening, species differences in κ/λ ratios, factors affecting λLC generation, and background on Kidins220 as a scaffold protein involved in receptor signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C8-C36 represent established knowledge from the literature, properly cited with appropriate references. These claims provide necessary background context for understanding the experimental work and are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: Single-cell sequencing confirms preferential recombination of Iglv1 in both WT and B-KO mice, consistent with the cooperative function of λ1-3 and λ2-4 enhancers. B-KO mice show relative increase in λ3-family usage compared to λ2-family, suggesting recombination of Igl-V-gene segments 5' of the λ2-4 enhancer is more dependent on Kidins220 than others.
results.evaluation: Claims C186-C188, C191-C192, C194-C195 are supported by sequencing data (Figure 1) and integrate established knowledge about Igl locus organization with the new findings. The interpretation that λ2-family recombination is more Kidins220-dependent is a reasonable inference from the data showing differential usage patterns.

results.result: The discussion integrates findings with prior literature showing that λLC B cell generation is more sensitive to defects in pre-BCR/BCR signaling. Kidins220-deficiency dampens receptor signaling in multiple cell types. The defective coupling of (pre-)BCR to MAPK/ERK pathway in B-KO cells results in insufficient upregulation of RAG and E2A proteins, with the Igl locus requiring higher E2A activity than Igk.
results.evaluation: Claims C196-C208 represent integration of the current findings with established literature, properly cited. The mechanistic interpretation linking reduced ERK signaling to insufficient RAG/E2A expression is a reasonable inference supported by the data (reduced pERK in Figure 8D, reduced Tcf3 and Rag2 in Figure 4E) and prior literature.

results.result: The discussion proposes a mechanistic model where reduced ROS in Kidins220-deficient B cells leads to higher ERK phosphatase activity and reduced ERK phosphorylation. ROS and MAPK/ERK pathways are interconnected, and ROS can activate ERK and inactivate phosphatases. The model proposes Kidins220 enhances pre-BCR and BCR signaling, though direct effects on Igl locus opening cannot be ruled out.
results.evaluation: Claims C209-C217 represent a mechanistic model integrating the ROS and ERK data with established literature. While the model is plausible and supported by the observed correlations (reduced ROS and reduced pERK in B-KO cells), the causal relationship between ROS and ERK phosphorylation in this context is not directly demonstrated. The authors appropriately acknowledge uncertainty (C217).

results.result: The discussion proposes that Kidins220 contributes to pre-B cell survival through connections between (pre-)BCR signaling and survival pathways, including NF-κB/Pim2 and ERK/BIM/BCL2 pathways. The incomplete rescue by BCL2 overexpression suggests prolonged survival is necessary but not sufficient for optimal λLC B cell generation in the absence of Kidins220.
results.evaluation: Claims C218-C227 integrate the survival data (increased apoptosis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, incomplete BCL2 rescue in Figures 4-5) with established literature on survival pathways. The conclusion that survival is necessary but not sufficient is directly supported by the BCL2 rescue experiments showing incomplete restoration of λLC+ B cells.

results.result: The discussion integrates receptor editing findings with established knowledge about κ vs λLC properties in rescuing autoreactive BCRs. The κ-macroself data demonstrate successful tolerance induction (elimination of κLC+ BCRs) but impaired λLC generation in B-KO mice, even with BCL2 overexpression. This is consistent with the repertoire analysis showing no signs of autoreactive BCRs in B-KO mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C228-C234 integrate the κ-macroself data (Figures 6-7) with established literature and the repertoire analysis (Figure 1). The interpretation that Kidins220 is essential for λLC generation during receptor editing but not for tolerance induction is directly supported by the data.

results.result: The discussion notes that since B-KO cells don't efficiently open the Igl locus, secondary Igk rearrangement should increase. This is supported by a slight increase in Igkj5 usage in B-KO mice (14.2% vs 10% in CTRL), which is associated with multiple rounds of secondary rearrangement before Igk locus silencing.
results.evaluation: Claims C235-C237 connect the sequencing data showing increased Igkj5 usage (Figure 1E) with established knowledge about Igkj5 and secondary rearrangements. The inference that increased Igkj5 usage reflects increased secondary rearrangement attempts is reasonable and supported by prior literature.

results.result: The study concludes that the heightened sensitivity of the Igl locus (compared to Igk) to reductions in recombination machinery proteins regulated by pre-BCR/BCR signals explains why Kidins220 absence specifically impacts Igl gene rearrangement. This adds to understanding of differential κ and λLC expression and self-tolerant repertoire generation.
results.evaluation: Claims C239 and C240 represent the final conclusions integrating all findings with established literature. The explanation for Igl-specific effects based on differential sensitivity is well-supported by the collective data showing normal Igk but impaired Igl recombination, and is consistent with prior literature on LC locus sensitivity.
